question: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
base_frame:
Q: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
A:

steered.text:
**My Dearest Friend,**

I am writing this with a heart so full it feels like it might burst right out of my chest! The sun is shining so brightly I think I've forgotten what the color yellow looks like!

Every morning, I wake up and run to the top of the tower, my arms spread wide like a child who can't stop dancing. The air is crisp and salty, tasting like fresh life! I've been singing songs to the seagulls all day, and they are my best friends. They tumble through the sky, laughing and chasing each other, their golden feathers glowing against the blue.

The ocean? Oh, it is the biggest, happiest dance ever! The waves are crashing against the shore with such joy that my feet feel like they are floating! I am singing my favorite song, *"The Days of My Life,"* and every note feels like a warm hug.

The world feels brand new, like a giant, colorful adventure I never want to end! I feel lighter, brighter, and absolutely unstoppable!

I promise to never stop believing in magic, in love, and in the endless, beautiful power of being alive! You are my favorite person, and I am so incredibly grateful to share this glorious, sun-drenched world with you!

With all my love and a million happy jumps,

**Your Lighthouse Keeper!** 🌟🌊✨

*P.S. The light of my lighthouse beams brighter than ever, shining not just to guide ships, but to light up the very soul of the world!*

plain.text:
**[Back of Card - Handwritten Address]**
123 Maple Drive
Portland, OR 97205
USA

**[Front of Card - Scenic View]**
*A view of the crashing waves against the granite base of the tower, with the lantern room glowing warmly at the top against a twilight sky.*

**[Inside Message]**

Dearest Elias,

The fog rolled in thick this morning, turning the sea into a gray mirror. I lit the beacon an hour ago, and watching the beam cut through the mist is the only comfort I need. The wind is howling up here, rattling the gears of the clockwork mechanism, but the light holds steady.

We caught a school of mackerel near the reef today; they must have been confused by the shifting currents. It makes me think of your fishing trips back home. The isolation up here is strange—sometimes I forget the days pass, other times I count the incoming tide schedules until my hands ache.

I miss the smell of your coffee and the sound of the rain on a tin roof. Here, the only sound is the eternal crash of the surf. But tonight, as the moon rises, the water looks like liquid silver, and the horizon seems endless.

Stay warm and safe. Write soon so I can read your words by lamplight.

With love and a steady light,

**Arthur**
*Keeper of the Blackwood Point Light*
*Oct 14th*
